pages.title: Carlucci American International School of Lisbon
blocks: A community where every student belongs.

CAISL is a student-centered educational community in which we challenge ourselves and each other to do our best and to make positive contributions to our diverse and ever-changing world. Families choose CAISL for a community where every child is known, challenged, and inspired to grow — academically, socially, and personally.
What does it mean to be part of an American international community? At CAISL, we want every person to feel like they belong.
From its beginnings in a small apartment in 1956 to a vibrant international campus today, CAISL’s journey reflects 70 years of growth, innovation, and commitment to American education in Portugal.
In 1956, with just 9 students in a small apartment in Pedrouços, Anthony McKenna founded a school with a big vision: bringing American education to Portugal.
As the community expanded beyond serving American families, the Portuguese Ministry of Education officially recognized the school’s educational program.
With the creation of the Linhó campus, CAISL brought its divisions together in a purpose-built learning environment designed to support the "whole child".
From 9 students to now over 700, CAISL is a thriving international community, continuing its mission; of balanced education in academics, arts, and athletics.
Ready to give your child the opportunity to explore, learn, and thrive at every stage of their learning journey?
For many children, this is when they take their first steps into an exciting journey — learning with joy helps them feel confident, curious, and excited to learn.
As they continue their journey, students strengthen foundational skills and understanding, learning to grow with curiosity while exploring the world around them.
With growing independence, students begin to explore who they are, developing critical thinking, self-awareness, and meaningful connections.
Students get ready for tomorrow by setting goals and preparing for life beyond the classroom — shaping who they want to become along the way.

pages.title: Meet Us - Carlucci American International School of Lisbon
blocks: CAISL is a student-centered educational community in which we challenge ourselves and each other to do our best and to make positive contributions to our diverse and ever-changing world.
Welcome to CAISL and thank you for visiting us online. CAISL provides students with opportunities in and out of the classroom to move beyond their comfort levels and grow as individuals.
We understand that this begins by building caring connections with our students. Here at CAISL, we develop academic, athletic and artistic skills alongside good citizenship and positive leadership.

CAISL serves school-aged dependents of the local and international communities in the Lisbon area. We’re proud of the community created by our multi-cultural student body, caring teachers and supportive parents.
I invite you to peruse the pages of our website to learn more about our programs. Our staff is always on hand to clarify any questions but don’t hesitate to contact me if I can help any further.
All of our faculty are fluent English speakers, and about 70% of core subject teachers are native speakers or “program carriers,” having studied or taught within American schools.

Many educators build long careers at CAISL, while new teachers join each year, creating a faculty that is both experienced and dynamic. Though they bring diverse perspectives and teaching styles, all share common expectations: engaging students in active learning, differentiating instruction to meet individual needs, and inspiring a lifelong love of learning.
Aligned with the International Taskforce on Child Protection, CAISL follows rigorous recruitment and safeguarding practices to ensure a safe environment for every student.

At the start of the 2025–2026 school year, CAISL enrolled 755 students representing 62 nationalities . About one-third of our students hold more than one nationality, reflecting the diverse backgrounds that shape daily life on our campus.
1. USA | 32% 2. Portugal | 19% 3. Other English-speaking countries | 5% 4. Other nationalities | 44%
Numbers may change during the school year.
Building a Reputation of Excellence over Time
The CAISL community includes everyone who shares an interest in the success of our learners. All members of the community strive to help our learners become:
Creative Problem Solvers who use a wide variety of resources and strategies to meet life’s challenges.
Effective Communicators who express and interpret ideas using appropriate means.
Conscientious Contributors who are committed to service, show empathy, and act to make a positive impact on the lives of others.
Life-Long Learners who reflect upon their experiences and actively seek the knowledge and skills necessary for continuous personal growth.
Principled Individuals who take responsibility for their choices, act with integrity, and demonstrate respect for themselves, others, and the environment.
CAISL is accredited by the Middle States Association through July 2029, with a Program of Distinction in Art and Music and an endorsement in Responsible AI in Learning.
Authorized to offer the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme since 2000.
Permanent License from Portuguese Ministry of Education

Permanently licensed by the Portuguese Ministry of Education since 2003 to provide an American curriculum from Early Childhood through High School, awarding both the American High School Diploma and the IB Diploma.
As a not-for-profit organization, CAISL has been recognized by the U.S. Department of State— the only American school in Portugal with this designation.
Our school is also part of the following professional associations:
Associação de Estabelecimentos de Ensino Particular e Cooperativo
The Fundação Escola Americana de Lisboa Board of Trustees is composed of three members.

One trustee is appointed by Visteon Portuguesa, and two are appointed by the U.S. Embassy to Portugal — one a Foreign Service officer and a second locally based representative with ties to both the United States and Portugal.

The Board establishes school policy and oversees the school’s long-term direction, while delegating day-to-day operations to the school leadership. Trustees also provide governance and oversight in areas such as finance, personnel, communications, and strategic planning.
If you would like more detailed information on our governing foundation, click below:
FEAL - Fundação Escola Americana de Lisboa
Miguel Espírito Santo Silva de Mello (Board President)
The main responsibility of the Trustees is to hold the school “in trust” for the future.

With CAISL's new facilities and campus having been completed in 2011, the Trustees now focus on ensuring financial sustainability, long-term stability, and responsible governance, to preserve CAISL’s mission for future generations.
